items.followUp: Differentiate between a saturated solution and an unsaturated solution.

rubric.why: Identifies a dilute solution by its relatively low solute content.
rubric.description: States that a dilute solution contains a small amount of solute compared with the solvent or solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct comparison.

rubric.why: Identifies a concentrated solution by its relatively high solute content.
rubric.description: States that a concentrated solution contains a large amount of solute compared with the solvent or solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct comparison.

modelAnswer: A dilute solution contains a small amount of solute relative to the amount of solvent or solution.
A concentrated solution contains a large amount of solute relative to the amount of solvent or solution.

items.followUp: Define percentage by mass and write its formula.

rubric.why: Shows that percentage by mass compares solute mass with the total solution mass.
rubric.description: Defines % m/m as the mass of solute present in 100 parts by mass of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Gives the standard calculation for mass percentage.
rubric.description: Writes the formula: % m/m = (mass of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: % m/m is the mass of solute present in 100 parts by mass of solution.
% m/m = (mass of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100

items.followUp: How are anode rays produced? State four of their characteristics.

rubric.why: Describes the conditions under which cathode rays are produced.
rubric.description: States that cathode rays are produced in a discharge tube containing gas at low pressure when a high voltage is applied.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the production method and conditions.

rubric.why: Includes a fundamental observed property of cathode rays.
rubric.description: States that cathode rays travel in straight lines.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this characteristic.

rubric.why: Identifies the electrical nature of cathode rays.
rubric.description: States that cathode rays carry a negative charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this characteristic.

rubric.why: Shows how cathode rays respond to an electric field.
rubric.description: States that cathode rays are deflected towards the positive plate in an electric field.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this characteristic.

rubric.why: Includes another characteristic observed when cathode rays strike certain materials.
rubric.description: States that cathode rays produce fluorescence when they strike certain substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this characteristic.

modelAnswer: Cathode rays are produced in a discharge tube containing gas at low pressure when a high voltage is applied between its electrodes.
They travel in straight lines.
They carry a negative charge.
They are deflected towards the positive plate in an electric field.
They produce fluorescence when they strike certain substances.

items.followUp: Differentiate between an atom and an atomic ion, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Gives the defining charge property of a molecule.
rubric.description: Defines a molecule as a neutral group of two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: Provides a correct example of a neutral molecule.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a molecule, such as H₂O or O₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

rubric.why: Distinguishes an ion made of bonded atoms from a neutral molecule.
rubric.description: Defines a molecular ion as a group of bonded atoms carrying an overall positive or negative charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: Provides a correct example of a molecular ion.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a molecular ion, such as NH₄⁺ or SO₄²⁻.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: A molecule is a neutral group of two or more atoms chemically bonded together; for example, H₂O.
A molecular ion is a group of bonded atoms carrying an overall charge; for example, NH₄⁺.

items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and explain how it forms in sodium chloride.

rubric.why: States the defining feature of covalent bonding.
rubric.description: Defines a covalent bond as a bond formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Identifies the single-bond type and a suitable example.
rubric.description: Explains that a single covalent bond involves sharing one pair of electrons and gives an example such as H₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and example.

rubric.why: Identifies the double-bond type and a suitable example.
rubric.description: Explains that a double covalent bond involves sharing two pairs of electrons and gives an example such as O₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and example.

rubric.why: Identifies the triple-bond type and a suitable example.
rubric.description: Explains that a triple covalent bond involves sharing three pairs of electrons and gives an example such as N₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and example.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
A single covalent bond involves sharing one pair of electrons; for example, H₂.
A double covalent bond involves sharing two pairs of electrons; for example, O₂.
A triple covalent bond involves sharing three pairs of electrons; for example, N₂.

items.followUp: Define boiling point and explain how it is affected by atmospheric pressure.

rubric.why: Gives the equilibrium definition of vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid at a given temperature.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete definition.

rubric.why: States the effect of temperature on vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Explains that vapour pressure increases as temperature increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct trend.

rubric.why: States how the nature of the liquid affects its vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Explains that liquids with weaker intermolecular forces have higher vapour pressure, while stronger forces give lower vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid at a given temperature.
Vapour pressure increases as the temperature increases.
The nature of the liquid also affects vapour pressure: weaker intermolecular forces give a higher vapour pressure, while stronger forces give a lower vapour pressure.

items.followUp: What are alkali metals? Describe how their reactivity changes down Group 1.

rubric.why: Identifies the group containing the halogens.
rubric.description: States that halogens are the elements of Group VIIA (Group 17).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the group.

rubric.why: Adds defining properties of the halogen elements.
rubric.description: States that halogens are non-metals and occur as diatomic molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for these properties.

rubric.why: Explains how halogens act as oxidizing agents.
rubric.description: States that halogen atoms gain electrons to form halide ions, thereby oxidizing other substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the electron-gain explanation.

rubric.why: Gives the trend in oxidizing strength within the group.
rubric.description: States that oxidizing power decreases down the group: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct order.

modelAnswer: Halogens are the non-metal elements of Group VIIA (Group 17); they occur as diatomic molecules.
Halogens are oxidizing agents because their atoms gain electrons to form halide ions.
Their oxidizing power decreases down the group: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.

items.followUp: Define organic chemistry and give one example of a process it studies.

rubric.why: Defines the subject in terms of chemistry in living things.
rubric.description: Defines biochemistry as the study of chemical compounds and processes in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: Provides an example of a biochemical process.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example, such as digestion, photosynthesis, or respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example.

modelAnswer: Biochemistry is the study of chemical compounds and processes in living organisms.
For example, it studies digestion.
